assumptions: This review uses only the supplied packet; no tools, files or commands were accessed.
Workers and controller are trusted, and containment covers only the initial process group and ordinary handled interruption.

Missing interface assumption: runtime_json and event are not shown to run exclusively inside an enclosing defer_shutdown context. The findings below concern their supplied implementations and visible call sites.
checks: Traced worker admission, role validation, configuration inspection, response validation and final integrity checks.
Examined runtime-record publication against ordinary handled interruption.
Compared editable-worker phase validation with the stated requirement that worker launch enforce proposal eligibility and declared write scope.
Treated the reported 218 passing tests as supporting control-plane evidence only; test bodies were not supplied.
evidence: scripts/run_accounting_master.py: Master.runtime_json, Master.event, Master.process, Master.worker and Master.check_runtime.
scripts/accounting_master_support.py: atomic_json durably publishes bytes before returning.
docs/plans/accounting-master-program.md: ordinary interruption/resume, exact supervisor-write tracking and phase-specific write-scope requirements.
tests/test_accounting_master.py: supplied test names cover runtime mutation and interruption, but do not establish coverage of interruption between runtime publication and expected-hash update.
issues: Runtime publication and its expected-hash update are interruptible separately. In runtime_json, atomic_json can replace the destination before runtime_expected is updated; in event, the append can complete before its expected hash is updated. An ordinary handled SIGTERM/KeyboardInterrupt in either interval leaves legitimate supervisor bytes different from the recorded expectation. The subsequent process cleanup or worker finally calls check_runtime and converts the interruption into a ContinuationVeto alleging an outside write; cleanup status publication can also fail for the same reason. Repair: defer handled shutdown across each complete check/write/expected-hash-update/check transaction, including event append, flush and fsync. Keep actual publication failures fail-closed. Add focused interruption tests at the publication-to-hash-update boundary for both methods, verifying cleanup and resumable interruption without a false integrity accusation.

Master.worker fails open for editable roles with an unknown phase ID. Both the phase_block check and the final declared-write-scope check execute only when phase['id'] is in self.phases. Consequently, worker('implement', unknown_phase, ...) or worker('repair', unknown_phase, ...) passes role validation, receives workspace-write access, and can change any inventoried file outside the globally protected controls without a phase-scope veto. This contradicts the stated worker-launch boundary and can arise from an ordinary erroneous caller; no hostile actor is needed. Repair: reject editable roles unless the phase ID is registered and passes phase_block, before writing budgets or launching queries. Explicitly allow only the required non-phase read-only roles. Add tests showing an unknown editable phase is rejected before launch and cannot bypass write-scope enforcement.
next_actions: Make runtime publication and expected-hash bookkeeping one shutdown-deferred transaction.
Require registered, eligible phases for every editable worker invocation.
Run focused regressions and the existing controller suite, then obtain a fresh bounded review of the repaired boundary.
residuals: Process-group cleanup internals, signal-context implementations, scheduler callers and approval-rule implementation were not included; their broader guarantees remain interface assumptions in this packet review.

The supplied source protections and acceptance interfaces preserve the distinction between 192 accepted reports, scoped internal acceptance and unresolved accounting, scientific and human-acceptance gaps.
The packet does not establish accounting correctness, substantive manuscript adequacy or human acceptance.
steps: Reviewed the supplied worker-boundary code against its stated interfaces.
Identified two repairable boundary defects without extending the threat model.
summary: REVISE: ordinary interruption can falsely trigger runtime-integrity vetoes, and unknown phase IDs bypass editable-worker phase and write-scope enforcement.
